1.note: Yedidyah the Alexandrian is Philo; the work is De aeternitate mundi.

2.note: Gsinofonti = Xenophon. 'On Equivocal Names' is the pseudo-Xenophontic De aequivocis published by Annius of Viterbo.

3.note: Ovid, Metamorphoses 12, probably Nestor's account of living through a third age (saeculum).

4.note: The verses quoted are Dan 7:14 and 7:18, in chapter 7, not 8; the author's number is kept.

5.note: Unclear editorial parenthesis, apparently a variant reading in the Mantua and Berlin editions; the sense of לודאי here is uncertain.

6.note: Augustine, City of God 22.30; Thomas Aquinas, Commentary on the Sentences IV.

7.note: Probably Hermannus Contractus, whose chronicle was printed with Eusebius' Chronicle; the identification is not certain.

8.note: The passage corresponds to the myth of the cosmic reversal in Plato's Statesman (269c ff.).

9.note: Timaeus 38b; the following speech is from Timaeus 41a-b; cited via Eusebius, Praeparatio Evangelica.

10.note: Leone Ebreo (Judah Abravanel), Dialoghi d'amore, third dialogue.

11.note: Mekor Hayyim is presumably Samuel Zarza's supercommentary on Ibn Ezra.

12.note: Philo, De opificio mundi 103-105, quoting Solon's elegy on the ten hebdomads of human life.
